titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §253: The Altan Qan Submits, and Qasar Takes the Border Cities
part: §253 — The Altan Qan Submits, and Qasar Takes the Border Cities
about: The Altan Qan, in Nanjing, submits and sends his son to serve as Chinggis's guard (§253). Chinggis withdraws by the Chabchiyal Pass and sends Qasar with the left wing along the sea to take Beijing and the Jurchen Buqanu, and then to rejoin him at the great camp. Grammar to watch: the long converb chains in -žu/-žü; causatives in -ġül-/-γ̇ul-; the reflexive -(i)jen; the plural optative -dqun/-dkün; and the Ming glossators' Chinese place names (Nanjing, the Juyong Pass, Daning).

sentences.t: Altan Qān Nangiṅ orožu öġer(i)-jen elsen mürügüžü
sentences.l: Altan Qan, Nanjing entering, own submitting, bowing,
sentences.i: The Altan Qan entered Nanjing, submitted of his own accord, bowed to the ground,
sentences.n: The first unit opens a chain: orožu (oro- ‘enter’ + -žu; Ming 入着), then öġer(i)-jen elsen (‘own, submitting’: öġer + the reflexive -(i)jen, Ming 自己 自的行; elsen is else- ‘submit’ + converb -n, Ming 歸附), then mürügüžü (stem inferred from Ming 叩頭 ‘kowtowing’). Altan Qān is the Jin emperor (Ming 金 皇帝, ‘Jin emperor’); Nangiṅ is the southern capital, Ming 汴梁 (Kaifeng). The verb is in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Altan, gold; here the title of the Jin emperor (Altan Qaγan), a name and title [金]
ruler, sovereign, khan (title; the short form after a name) [皇帝]
Nanjing (Han 南京), the Jin southern capital, Kaifeng (Ming 汴梁) [汴梁]
own, self (the (i) is Shiratori's linking vowel) [自己(自的行)]
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming) [歸附]
to bow, strike the head to the ground (stem inferred; Ming 叩頭) [叩頭着]

sentences.t: Teṅgeri neretü köġü-ben žaγ̇un nöködtü-ji Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur turγaγ boltuγai keġen iležüġü.
sentences.l: Tengeri named son-his-own, hundred companion-having-(object), Chinggis Qahan-to guard let-be saying, sent.
sentences.i: “Let his son named Tengeri, with a hundred companions, be a guard for Chinggis Qahan,” he said, and sent him.
sentences.n: Teṅgeri here is a man’s name (Ming 人名), the Altan Qan’s son: neretü is nere ‘name’ + possessive -tü (‘having the name’). köġü-ben is ‘son’ + the reflexive -ben, ‘his own son’. žaγ̇un nöködtü-ji is ‘a hundred companion-having’, with the accusative -ji (Ming 伴當有的行); I read it as the son’s retinue, not as a second object. turγaγ boltuγai is ‘let (him) be a guard’ (-tuγai optative, Ming 做者). keġen is ke- ‘say’ + -ġen, Ming 麽道, which closes the quotation. iležüġü (Ming 敎來了) is ‘sent’; the ending is unusual. Shiratori marks neither the opening nor the closing of the speech; I supply the marks in `i` only.

morph.gloss: Tengeri, Heaven; here a man's name (Ming 人名) [人名]
son (short form of köġün) [兒子自的行]
companion (nökör, plural nököd) [伴當(每)有的行]
Chinggis (Shiratori's spelling), a man's name [太祖︀]
optative: let it be, let him be (third person, back-vowel form)
past tense (Ming 來了; a rare ending)

sentences.t: Ima-da elsegdežü Čiṅgis Qaγan ičuja keġen
sentences.l: Him-to submission-having-been-made, Chinggis Qahan let-us-withdraw saying,
sentences.i: When he had been brought to submit, Chinggis Qahan said, “Let us withdraw,”
sentences.n: Ima-da is a pronoun stem + dative-locative -da (Ming 他 行, ‘to him’). elsegdežü is else- ‘submit’ + passive -gde- + -žü; the Ming 被歸附着 ‘being submitted’ shows that the Altan Qan’s submission is what has been done to him. ičuja is read from the Ming 退咱 (‘let us withdraw’; the ending is taken as a hortative and is uncertain). keġen again closes a quotation.

morph.gloss: he, that one (a pronoun stem, Ming 他) [他 行]
let us withdraw (ičü-/ičuγa- 'withdraw, retreat', from the Ming 退; ending uncertain) [退咱]

sentences.t: Čabčijal(i)-jar tende ičurun Qasar-i žeġün γar-un čeriġüd(i)-jer dalai kižin ilerün
sentences.l: Chabchiyal-by there withdrawing, Qasar-(object) left hand’s troops-with sea along sending,
sentences.i: “As we withdraw by the Chabchiyal Pass, send Qasar with the troops of the left wing along the sea,
sentences.n: Čabčijal(i)-jar is the Juyong Pass (Ming 居庸關 依着) with the instrumental -(i)jar, ‘by, along’. ičurun (Ming 退時) is a converb ‘while withdrawing’. Qasar-i is accusative, and ilerün is ile- ‘send’ + -run: the one who sends is Chinggis, who is therefore speaking, which is why I supply the opening quotation mark here, in `i` only. žeġün γar-un čeriġüd(i)-jer is ‘left-hand’s troops-by’, the left wing (Ming 左手的軍每敎). kižin (Ming 㳂) ‘along the edge of’.

morph.gloss: Chabchiyal, the Juyong Pass (Ming 居庸關) [居庸關 依着]
to withdraw (from the Ming 退) [退時]
Qasar, a man's name (Chinggis's brother) [人名 行]
instrumental: with, by means of (the (i) is Shiratori's)
along the edge of, following the shore (Ming 㳂) [㳂]

sentences.i: and bring down the city of Beijing.
sentences.n: Bēgiṅ is Ming 北京 and, glossed 大寗, the Daning of the Jin (the Liao-Jin Central Capital), not modern Beijing; I write ‘Beijing’ as the Ming writes it. baγudqun (baγu- ‘come down’, Ming 下您) is read as an imperative to several people: ‘bring (it) down’, i.e. take the city. The ending -dqun is uncertain.

morph.gloss: Beijing (Daning, Ming 大寗), a city [大寗]
to descend, come down (Ming 下, of taking a city) [下您]

sentences.t: Bēgiṅ balaγasan-i elšeġülžü činana Žürčed-ün Buqanu-ji daγ̇arin odču
sentences.l: Beijing city-(object) submission-causing, beyond Jurchen’s Buqanu-(object) passing going,
sentences.i: Make the city of Beijing submit, then go on beyond it, passing by Buqanu of the Jurchen.
sentences.n: elšeġülžü is else- ‘submit’ + causative -ġül- + -žü, Ming 敎歸附着 ‘having made submit’. činana (Ming 那廂) ‘on that side, beyond’. Žürčed-ün Buqanu-ji is ‘the Jurchen’s Buqanu’ with the accusative -ji (Ming 人名 行); the Jurchen are named in Chinese 女眞. daγ̇arin odču is ‘passing, going’ (Ming 經過, 去着).

morph.gloss: on that side, beyond (adverb, Ming 那廂) [那廂]
to pass through, go by (Ming 經過) [經過]

sentences.i: If Buqanu plans rebellion, put him down; if he submits,
sentences.n: bulγa (Ming 反) is ‘rebellion’; sedkiġesü is sedki- ‘think’ + conditional -ġesü (Ming 想呵). qaγ̇uludqun is read from the Ming 勦捕您 ‘hunt down and seize’: stem qaγ̇ulu- and the same ending -dqun as in baγudqun. elseġesü is else- + -ġesü (Ming 歸附呵). The two conditions balance each other.

morph.gloss: to hunt down, put down (Ming 勦捕) [勦捕您]

sentences.t: in-ü kižiγ̇ar balaγad an-u daγ̇arin Ula, Naγ̇u müred kižin odču
sentences.l: his edge cities his passing, Ula, Naγu rivers along going,
sentences.i: pass by the border cities of his, and go along the rivers Ula and Naghu,
sentences.n: in-ü and an-u are the pronoun ‘his’ + genitive (Ming 他的); kižiγ̇ar (Ming 邊) is ‘edge, border’ and balaγad is the plural of balaγasun ‘city’, so ‘his border cities’. daγ̇arin is again ‘passing’ (Ming 經過). Ula and Naγ̇u are rivers (Ming 河名); müred is müren ‘river’ in the plural (Ming 河每); kižin odču ‘going along’. The English names of the rivers are as the Mongol writes them.

morph.gloss: he, that one (Ming 他; pronoun stem) [他的]
he, that one (Ming 他; pronoun stem) [他的]
to pass through, go by [經過]
along the edge of, following (Ming 㳂) [㳂]

sentences.t: Taγ̇ur müren öġede dabažu jeke aγ̇uruγ-tur neilen iredkün" keġežü
sentences.l: Taγur river against crossing, great camp-at joining let-them-come saying,
sentences.i: cross the Taghur river against its flow, and gather at the great camp,” he said.
sentences.n: Taγ̇ur müren is ‘the Taγur river’ (Ming 河名 河); öġede (Ming 逆着) is ‘against’, i.e. upstream, ‘against the stream’; dabažu is daba- ‘cross’ + -žu (Ming 越着). aγ̇uruγ-tur (Ming 營盤 裏) is ‘in the camp’. neilen is ‘joining’ (Ming 相合). iredkün (ire- ‘come’ + -dkün, Ming 來您) is ‘let them come’; Shiratori closes the quotation here, on iredkün, and keġežü (Ming 說着) is ‘saying’. This closing mark is the only quotation mark in the section.

morph.gloss: against, facing, upstream (Ming 逆着) [逆着]
to cross over, pass over [越着]
to join together, meet (Ming 相合) [相合]
plural prohibitive/optative: let them come (Ming 來您)

sentences.n: irebe is ire- ‘come’ + -be (Ming 來了): the subject, unnamed, is Chinggis, who gave the orders and came to the camp. A short unit on purpose, to hold the verb.

sentences.t: Qasar-luγ̇a nojad-ača Žürčedei, Alči, Tolun čerbi γurban-i ileldübe.
sentences.l: Qasar-with officers-from Jürchedei, Alchi, Tolun cherbi, three-(object) sent-together.
sentences.i: With Qasar he sent along three of the officers, Jürchedei, Alchi and Tolun the cherbi.
sentences.n: Qasar-luγ̇a is ‘with Qasar’ (comitative -luγ̇a; Ming 一同). nojad-ača is noyan ‘lord’ in the plural with the ablative ‘from among the officers’ (Ming 官人每行). Three names then γurban-i ‘the three’ + accusative. čerbi is an office (Ming 官名). ileldübe (Ming 敎共去了) is ile- ‘send’ + -ldü- ‘together’ + -be. The chronicler lists Jürchedei, Alchi and Tolun after a comma each in Shiratori; I have kept the three names as in the print.

morph.gloss: Qasar, a man's name [人名 一同]
lord, officer (plural nojad; Ming 官人每) [官人每行]
cherbi, an office (Ming 官名) [官名]

sentences.t: Qasar Bēgiṅ balaγasun oroγ̇ulžu Žürčed-ün Buqanu-ji elseġülžü mör-e bümüi balaγasan-i oroγ̇uluγ̇ad
sentences.l: Qasar Beijing city entering-causing, Jurchen’s Buqanu-(object) submission-causing, road-on being city-(object) entering-causing,
sentences.i: Qasar made the city of Beijing yield, made Buqanu of the Jurchen submit, and made the cities that lay on the road surrender,
sentences.n: oroγ̇ulžu (Ming 敎投降着) is oro- ‘enter’ + causative -γ̇ul- + -žu, ‘making enter’, i.e. ‘making surrender’. elseġülžü is as before (Ming 敎歸附着). mör-e bümüi balaγasan-i is ‘road-on being city-(object)’, Ming 路行 有的 城子 行, ‘the cities that are on the road’; oroγ̇uluγ̇ad (Ming 敎投入了) is the same causative with -γ̇ad. I take the first Qasar as the doer of all three clauses.

sentences.t: Qasar Taγ̇ur müren öġede irežü jeke aγ̇uruγ-tur baγ̇užu irebe.
sentences.l: Qasar Taγur river against coming, great camp-at descending, came.
sentences.i: Then Qasar came up the Taghur river and halted at the great camp.
sentences.n: Qasar (Ming 人名) is the subject of the whole chain. Taγ̇ur müren öġede irežü is ‘coming against the Taγur river’ (Ming 逆着 來着); baγ̇užu (Ming 下着) is ‘alighting’ and irebe the closing verb. aγ̇uruγ-tur is ‘at the camp’ (Ming 營盤 裏), as in unit 9. The section ends here.
